newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index drops from record territory.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index drops from record territory.

text.p: Kuwait share index eased 1.76 percent to 1919.9 in the week to Wednesday after a long upward trend set new records in recent weeks.

"I have doubts that this is a major correction process...The situation deserves a correction, and the sooner it comes the lesser the losses would be," leading economist Jassem al-Saadoun said of the 34.3 point index drop this week.
Some market analysts have been expecting a correction on the Kuwait Stock Exchange. The index rose 218.4 points in October month-on-month to 1,954.2, a 43 percent increase from January 2.

Trade volume dropped this week to 900 million shares, a daily average of 180 million, from 965 million shares last week. Value edged up to 287.2 million dinars ($960.5 million), a daily average of 57.44 million dinars, from 285.5 million dinars.
Dealers said the market was active in profit taking on Tuesday when the index dropped 43.9 points to 1920.4. Last week the index rose 76.3 points or four percent.
Loosers led gainers 37-12 this week, five were non-movers and four reported no trade.
Gulf Insurance Co registered the largest fall of 70 fils to 640 fils. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.

The largest gain was recorded by Mobile Telecommunications Co whose share rose 140 fils in the week to 1.140 dinars. It was also among the most traded shares by value along with National Bank of Kuwait, Commercial Bank of Kuwait and Investment Projects.
By sector, banks led trading by value accounting for 35.8 percent, followed by investment firms with 21.34 percent and industrials with 14.4 percent.
Investment firms were the most active sector by volume with 30.5 percent, followed by banks with 24.8 percent and property shares with 17.9 percent.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
